sections.future_developments: Future developments The directors continue to monitor the economic and political changes challenges left in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, as well as the significant operation challenges created through disruption to the global supply chain. The directors believe the group remains well placed in the market and, through continued focus on value driven products, the group will be well positioned to take opportunities in the market as they become available. Further investment into products, systems, owned websites and the company’s wholly owned IP help differentiate the company’s offering helping to ensure that long term equity value is being built into the business. The group have also invested in integrations to new marketplaces to ensure their product is on sale where the customer shops. The global supply chain is now showing signs of returning to normal, with freight rates returning to pre-pandemic levels, factory lead times shortening and commodity prices stabilizing. These factors have weighed heavily on the business, and as these ease, the group can start to return to normalised levels of profitability. Although the business became an Employee Owned Trust in early 2021, the business recognises the transition is a journey, an establishing the Trust structure is only the first step. The company will continue to work with its employees to learn what it means to be an EOT, and ensure that the transition delivers on its goals of increasing employee engagement, aligning corporate and strategic goals, and driving sustainable, profitable growth. On behalf of the board M R Januszewski Director 19 May 2025 DOMU BRANDS LIMITED
sections.principal_activity: Principal activities Domu Brands is a home and lifestyle ecommerce retailer based in the UK, dedicated to delivering great value, design led functional products, alongside a fantastic customer experience. The group operates through dedicated brand websites and via strategic partnerships with several well-known online marketplaces, to bring its products to market. Review of the business The financial year ending September 2024 was a positive year for DOMU Brands Ltd, with the business returning to profit and achieving an EBITDA of £3.2m. The macro-economic environment continued to be uncertain, however through greater control and focus on our operational performance we were able to adapt and maintain strong results. YOY revenue remained stable at £44m, when factoring in the longer accounting period for FY23. However, this is now much higher quality revenue when compared to previous years. As we move in to FY25 and beyond we are planning controlled and consistent YOY revenue growth of this quality revenue. There continues to be cost pressures within the business, including those caused by government policy and more general inflationary pressured. However, we still aim to grow our bottom line faster than we grow the top line, through greater focus on efficiency and productivity. The future is looking very positive for DOMU Brands and its fantastic team. Performance Group revenue was reduced by 20.2% to £44.4m (FY23 £55.8m) reflecting the shorter accounting period and exit from the USA Market. Gross margin increased due to improved performance during year, increasing to £11.0m in FY 24 (FY22 £10.2m) which is an increase of £0.8m. 2024 £ 2023 £ EBITDA Adjustment Net Profit/(Loss) 2,588,345 (1,945,824) Depreciation and amortisation 315,936 470,985 Interest 339,746 490,559 EBITDA 3,244,027 (984,280) EBITDA 3,244,027 (984,280) The fixed cost base reduced due to improved operational efficiency, by £3.5m in FY24 (-30%). The combination of increased Gross margin and reduced operating cost saw the EBITDA performance improve by £4.2m year on year. Cash at period end was £1.7m in FY24. To support purchase of imports from overseas suppliers, the business deploys an import loan facility of $4m US dollars. The import loan facility balance at September 2024 stood at £2.9m. The business, due to focus on stock control, now successfully operates within a $6m dollar facility. DOMU BRANDS LIMITED
sections.principal_risks: Principal risks and uncertainties The group operates in a competitive marketplace, and maintains competitive advantage through good stock availability, excellent customer service and quality and range of product. Stock obsolescence risk is managed through closely monitoring slow moving lines and taking prompt action to clear through these lines. The severe global headwinds caused by the ongoing Trade tensions between the USA and China continue to create a volatile environment to operate within. Domu Brands’ core business model remains resilient through diversification of routes to market whilst always offering desirable and functional products that continue to resonate strongly with customers. Products are predominantly sourced from Asia and are priced and paid for in USD. However, diversification of the supply chain is a growing area of focus, with the business onboarding new partners in new countries. Through long term relationships with suppliers, cost pressures and competition for production space risk is managed. The impact of exchange rate movements because of pricing product in USD remains a key risk for the business. At the balance sheet date the group entered into forward rate contracts to mitigate risk to the business. As at the date of signing, the group has secured forward contracts to fully cover the majority of the SS25 range, and a portion of AW26 The group manages operational risk through its reporting systems and produces timely and accurate management information which is consistently reviewed by management. Facility headroom is closely monitored, with sensitisations around revenue and stock being modelled as part of the forecasting process. The company’s forecasts and projections show the group will be able to operate well within the level of the current import loan facility, which has been agreed through to 30th September 2025. This allows the Directors to conclude that there is reasonable expectation that the company has adequate resources to continue in operational existence for the foreseeable future. Banking facilities for the following financial year are due to be renewed in September 2025. Based on the company’s ability to manage through these dynamic conditions while reducing the debt facility alongside improving profitability, and after review of latest forward projections, our banking partners indicate that there will be no problem renewing import loan facilities at the current level. sections.strategic_report: STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED) FOR THE YEAR ENDED 30 SEPTEMBER 2024 \- 5 - The global supply chain challenges created an opportunity to identify and deliver energy efficiency savings in the extended journey from port to UK warehouse. Some of these initiatives included reducing the average CBM across the product portfolio, increasing shipping utilisation in containers from 94% to 96%. Product sample assessments have been majority offshored to remove unnecessary airfreight costs, with some studio production also being offshored to support this initiative. Finally, a greater weighting of containers landed through the Port of Liverpool, effectively removing 430 miles from every round trip to the warehouse. The company continues to strive to deliver energy saving initiatives, and at the end of FY22 the company agreed to exit one of the head office floors to consolidate all head office functions onto the remaining two floors. This resulted in utility and energy costs being reduced by 37% based on square footage. This is in addition to deploying a hybrid working model for all head office functions saving a further 40% in heating costs. Business travel was also kept to a minimum, with the group employees embracing video conferencing to key supplier, vendor and channel teams. We will continue to assess energy saving practices. Section 172(1) Statement The Directors of the group, as those of all UK companies, must act in accordance with a set of general duties. The Directors consider its shareholders, employees, customers, suppliers and local community to be its core stakeholder groups. The duties are detailed in section 172 of the UK Companies Act 2006 which is summarised as follows: ‘A director of a company must act in the way they consider, in good faith, would be most likely to promote the success of the company for the benefit of its shareholders as a whole and, in doing so have regard (amongst other matters) to the following areas: The likely consequence of any decision in the long term The interests of the company’s employees The need to foster the company’s business relationships with suppliers, customers and others The impact of the company’s operations on the community and the environment The desirability of the company maintaining a reputation for high standards or business conduct The need to act fairly as between members of the company’. The following points summarise how the Directors fulfil their duties:- S172(1) (A) “The likely consequence of any decision in the long term” The Board recognises the challenges facing the business from the macro and microenvironment. The Board meet monthly to discuss financial performance, forecasted outlook, future opportunities and key threats. The OKR framework is one key tool used by the business to assist with goal congruence throughout the business in order to achieve our operational, engagement and financial objectives. S172(1) (B) “The interests of the company’s employees” The Directors understands the importance of our employees, and the direct relationship between employee engagement and achieving long term success. This factor was at the forefront of the decision to transition the business to an Employee Owned Trust (EOT) in February 2021. This change in structure aims to allow employees, as sole beneficiaries of the Trust, to share in the future success of Domu Brands Limited The Directors and senior management team have a key focus on employee engagement, assessing results from the main survey once a year, with temperature checks throughout the year to ensure the current strategy is achieving what it set out to. The company strives to be a responsible employer and review pay, benefits and working environment on a regular basis. DOMU BRANDS LIMITED STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED) FOR THE YEAR ENDED 30 SEPTEMBER 2024 \- 6 - S172(1) (C) “The need to foster the company’s business relationships with suppliers, customers and others” The company remains focused on the successful growth of its own brand website. This effort is to ensure the customer journey is continually improved, reducing the likelihood for customer to return. Furthermore, the end-to-end supply chain needs constant evaluation, to ensure the customer is receiving great value for the service Domu provides. We frequently tender the services we receive from our suppliers and partners, to ensure they remain competitive, and their proposition aligns with the company’s core strategies. Our aim is to have a positive working relationship with all our partners and suppliers, this is predominantly lead through strong communication lines. Our stock suppliers have a dedicated member of the team to communicate with to resolve issues and queries. In addition, we are keen to meet with our suppliers on a frequent basis, even throughout the global pandemic, meetings over video conferencing software provided a similar personal feel. S172(1) (D) “The impact of the company’s operations on the community and the environment” The business has had to pivot on several occasions through the year as it worked through the unwinding of the COVID restrictions. One of the key measures was to implement a hybrid remote working policy, creating flexibility but also structure to allow employees to work from home when required, but also bringing teams together in a safe and secure environment. The board have also worked closely with stakeholders across the supply chain to limit the impact of the products journey from shipping through to end delivery. Steps included increasing utilisation of container ships, alongside product shrinkflation, localising QA checks in China, and landing containers at Liverpool port compared to Felixstowe.
